tasks.short: Assess manuscripts and recommend acceptance or revision to the publishing lead.

steps.what: Gather the manuscript, publication brief, review history and supporting sources.
Read closely for audience fit, originality, argument and editorial quality.
Check supporting sources, house style and gaps against the publication brief.

loop.input: Versioned manuscript, publication brief, style guide and approved source pack.
loop.output: Passage-linked findings separating rule violations, source gaps and uncertain editorial concerns.
loop.check: Run deterministic style rules; require valid passage references and source links; editor checks material findings.
loop.stop: One analysis and one repair pass per manuscript version; unresolved findings go to the editor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules handle spelling and terminology, but argument gaps and source support require reading prose.

steps.what: Decide whether to recommend acceptance or revision and set revision priorities.
Write the recommendation memo with reasons and actionable revision requests.

loop.input: Editor's recommendation, notes, verified findings and memo template.
loop.output: Recommendation memo with ranked revision requests and passage references.
loop.check: Preserve the selected recommendation; link each criticism to supplied evidence; editor checks tone and priorities.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision pass; unsupported statements are removed or returned for manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies structure, but clear explanations and revision requests depend on manuscript-specific prose.

steps.what: Check and send the recommendation memo to the publishing lead.

tasks.design: Configure the {CMS} to assemble a versioned review pack from the {DOCS}, run style rules and attach passage-linked findings from a bounded model loop. The editor reads the manuscript and chooses the recommendation; a second bounded loop drafts the memo, which the editor approves before routing through the {CMS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Files, source notes and review history were scattered. Templates could structure a memo but could not explain manuscript-specific concerns reliably.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing workflow features can assemble and route review packs. AI-assisted coding makes small connectors and validation checks cheaper to build; bounded drafting reduces memo preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Editorial merit, originality and reputational consequences remain contextual. Missing or unreliable sources still require investigation.
tasks.human_edge: The editor recognises a valuable unfamiliar voice, weighs the audience's needs and gives revision advice an author can use.

ambition.what: Early revision clinic for first-time internal subject-expert authors.

tasks.altitude: The editor spends less time assembling files and writing up findings, leaving room for earlier author coaching. Recommendation rights remain unchanged; the publishing lead retains the publication decision.

reach.task: Turn audience research into evidence for publication briefs.
reach.learn: Research sampling, audience segmentation and the limits of engagement metrics.

reach.task: Develop a revision plan before producing a full manuscript.
reach.learn: Author interviewing, argument structure and practical coaching.

evidence.claim: Repeatable house-style checks and quality gates are available today.
A controlled professional-writing trial supports drafting assistance, but does not establish reliable manuscript acceptance decisions.
A documented case of invented quotations supports checking generated claims against supplied sources.
The proposed workflow, time shares and build ranges are estimates, not documented results for this task.

assumptions: The publishing lead is the marketing publication owner in a mid-size European company.
Most manuscripts are reviewed in the {DOCS}; the {CMS} holds publication status and some history.
Close reading and the recommendation remain human despite the task's automation prior.
Build ranges cover one publication workflow and accessible interfaces; they are working-day effort estimates.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act obligations apply. Marketing work receives no assumed journalistic exemption.
Access planning includes employee consultation under national rules where applicable; no editor productivity monitoring is proposed.
unknowns: Where manuscript versions, review history and source packs are currently stored.
Who may recommend acceptance and who may approve publication.
Whether the style guide and publication criteria are explicit and current.
Which confidential or personal data may enter an approved model environment.
Available interfaces, access owners and applicable employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: How accurately can bounded checks identify unsupported claims and argument gaps across the intended manuscript types?
Which existing {CMS} features can replace custom routing and version assembly?
What current EU AI Act transparency obligations apply to the intended public-facing content?
new_work: Review passage-linked findings and discard weak criticisms.
Check draft memos for unsupported claims and altered priorities.
Maintain the style guide, review rubric and source-access rules.
Handle version conflicts and failed document links.
Sample completed reviews to detect missed issues and systematic bias.

tasks.short: Obtain and record copyright permissions for material planned for publication.

steps.what: Identify third-party passages, images and other material requiring a rights check.

loop.input: Manuscript, asset list, captions and supplied source references.
loop.output: Candidate third-party items with locations, source references and missing provenance flags.
loop.check: Match listed assets deterministically; require a manuscript location for each finding; editor checks inventory completeness.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per version; unresolved provenance remains flagged for manual investigation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Asset identifiers can be matched by rules, but embedded quotations and informal credits require reading.

steps.what: Find rights holders and check existing licences and permission records.
Decide whether permission is needed and define the requested use.
Prepare requests covering channels, territory, duration, adaptations and attribution.
Check the recipient and requested scope, then send the permission request.
Track responses and chase outstanding requests against publication deadlines.
Resolve fees, restrictions and disputed ownership with rights holders.
Read the grant and compare its conditions with the planned use.

loop.input: Permission agreement, complete correspondence and structured requested scope.
loop.output: Cited grant conditions, missing terms and scope mismatches.
loop.check: Require a source passage for each extracted condition; compare structured fields by rules; editor confirms interpretation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; ambiguity remains uncleared and goes to a legal reviewer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Grants arrive as varied prose and attachments; field matching alone cannot establish their stated conditions.

steps.what: Approve the clearance record and save conditions for publication and reuse.

tasks.design: Configure a rights register in the {CLM}, link evidence from the {DOCS}, and use the {WORKFLOW} to generate requests, track replies and send limited reminders through the {EMAIL}. Bounded extraction proposes inventory entries and grant conditions; approved clearance records feed restrictions and expiry checks into the {CMS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Permissions lived in attachments and mailbox threads, while the tracking sheet lacked reliable links to assets and publication scope. Legal meaning and ownership disputes resisted simple rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured request forms, existing workflow configuration and small integrations can remove repeated entry. Bounded extraction can turn varied grants into reviewable fields without deciding legal entitlement.
tasks.still_hard: Rights ownership, incomplete provenance, sublicensing and ambiguous grants remain difficult. External response time and negotiation do not disappear.
tasks.human_edge: The editor knows when to replace an asset, negotiate a restriction or involve a legal reviewer rather than accept uncertain rights.

ambition.what: Self-service discovery of previously cleared assets with visible reuse conditions.

tasks.altitude: The editor spends less time chasing replies and rebuilding permission histories, and more time resolving exceptions before deadlines. No new authority to commit fees or accept legal terms is assumed.

reach.task: Choose suitable assets that are already cleared for the planned channels.
reach.learn: Asset provenance, attribution requirements and channel-specific licence limits.

reach.task: Plan reuse of approved quotations and images across campaign materials.
reach.learn: Permission scope, adaptations, expiry and restrictions on onward distribution.

evidence.claim: Forms, template-generated requests, scheduled reminders and linked rights records can automate permission administration.
Extracting grant conditions can assist review, but cannot establish ownership or resolve ambiguous permission.
The digest provides no documented end-to-end copyright-clearance case; time shares and build ranges are estimates.

assumptions: The editor coordinates permissions and handles routine cases within delegated limits.
A {SPREADSHEET} commonly ties permission correspondence to publication plans; contracts may also sit in the {CLM}.
The answer desk uses configured search and asset identifiers; uncertain ownership still requires manual investigation.
Requests use structured scope fields and approved templates, so model drafting is unnecessary.
Automatic reminders use approved wording, the original recipient and unchanged scope, with a fixed limit and stop on reply.
Nonstandard terms and commitments outside delegated limits go to the legal reviewer or budget owner.
Build ranges cover one rights workflow and accessible interfaces; external rights-holder waiting time is excluded.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act obligations apply. Employee consultation follows national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Where existing grants, licences and asset identifiers are stored.
Whether the company already has a searchable rights register or reusable blanket licences.
Who can approve fees, accept restrictions and clear publication.
How often ownership is unclear or correspondence contains conflicting terms.
Available interfaces and whether reminder sending is authorised.
Access restrictions, retention requirements and applicable employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which existing {CLM} or {CMS} features support asset-level scope, attribution and expiry checks?
How reliably can grant extraction preserve exclusions and conflicting conditions across relevant languages?
Which national copyright rules and licence interpretations need specialist review for the intended uses?
new_work: Check extracted inventories and grant conditions against original evidence.
Resolve uncertain ownership and conflicting correspondence.
Maintain request templates, scope fields and reminder limits.
Review expiry alerts and changed publication uses.
Repair unmatched assets and failed correspondence links.
Maintain access controls and retention settings for rights-holder contact data.

role.altitude: The editor's week shifts from assembling evidence, writing routine memos and chasing permissions toward close reading, author coaching and difficult rights decisions. Publication, legal and spending authority remain with their existing owners unless explicitly delegated.
reach: Help writers shape revision plans earlier.
Use audience research to strengthen editorial briefs.
Help designers and public relations specialists find assets with suitable reuse rights.
skills_to_grow: Author coaching and constructive revision advice.
Evaluation of model findings and source fidelity.
role.ambitious_version: Run an editorial support service that offers first-time subject-expert authors early revision help and gives campaign teams a searchable collection of cleared assets.
